title: BOOL logic: AND, OR, NOT
summary: Combine signals with AND, OR, NOT and XOR to express machine conditions.
objectives: Use AND, OR, NOT and XOR
Read a condition as a sentence

sections.heading: Logic operators
sections.body: `A AND B` is TRUE only when both are TRUE. `A OR B` is TRUE when at least one is TRUE. `NOT A` inverts. `A XOR B` is TRUE when exactly one is TRUE. AND binds stronger than OR; use parentheses to make intent explicit.

sections.heading: Truth table
sections.diagram:
A     B     | A AND B | A OR B | A XOR B
  FALSE FALSE |  FALSE  | FALSE  |  FALSE
  FALSE TRUE  |  FALSE  | TRUE   |  TRUE
  TRUE  FALSE |  FALSE  | TRUE   |  TRUE
  TRUE  TRUE  |  TRUE   | TRUE   |  FALSE

sections.heading: Conditions as sentences
sections.body: 'The lamp is on when the button is pressed and the selector is in AUTO.'
sections.code:
Lamp1 := Button1 AND AutoMode;
Lamp3 := Button1 XOR Button2;  (* exactly one button pressed *)

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: `A OR B AND C` means `A OR (B AND C)`, not `(A OR B) AND C`. When in doubt, add parentheses.

question.question: Button1 = TRUE, Button2 = FALSE, AutoMode = FALSE. What is Button1 OR Button2 AND AutoMode?
question.explanation: AND first: FALSE AND FALSE = FALSE; then TRUE OR FALSE = TRUE.

sections.heading: Try combinations
sections.body: In the I/O panel, write a few conditions for Lamp1 to Lamp3 and test every combination of buttons and the selector.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
AND, OR, NOT and XOR express almost every machine condition; parentheses make them unambiguous.

**Troubleshooting note:** When a condition 'never becomes true', watch each operand in the Watch list; the false one is your lead.

checkpoint.question: When is A AND NOT B TRUE?
checkpoint.explanation: NOT B must be TRUE, so B is FALSE.

checkpoint.question: Which operator is TRUE for exactly one TRUE input?
